channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Falas de Lula já não atenuam dano político do caso Lulinha
item.description: Lula's statements can no longer contain the political damage caused by the Lulinha case, which has put corruption back at the center of the electoral debate. With the anti-corruption agenda gaining traction among voters, the president had to revisit the same repertoire used in the 2022 succession, when he admitted wrongdoing in a televised interview. The episode highlights the government's difficulty in shielding itself from scandals involving family members in an election year.

item.title: Pesquisa senador SP: veja números do levantamento RealTime Big Data
item.description: A RealTime Big Data poll released on August 24, 2026 shows a technical tie among four candidates in the São Paulo Senate race, within the two-percentage-point margin of error. Guilherme Derrite (PP) leads with 18%, followed by Simone Tebet (PSB) with 17%, André do Prado (PL) with 15%, and Marina Silva (Rede) with 14%. The survey interviewed 2,000 voters by phone between August 19 and 22 and was registered with the TSE under number SP-01347/2026.

item.title: Ao contrário de Bolsonaro, Lula não está protegendo o filho, diz Haddad
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), candidate for governor of São Paulo, stated during a UOL/Folha interview that President Lula is not protecting his son Fábio Luís Lula da Silva from Federal Police investigations. Haddad made a direct comparison with former president Jair Bolsonaro, implying that Bolsonaro acted differently by shielding his children from similar probes.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Ministro da Fazenda defende combater 'pejotização' para conter déficit da Previdência Social
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan defended combating 'pejotização' (hiring workers as contractors instead of formally employed) to reduce the Social Security deficit, proposing rules on the percentage of PJ workers allowed in companies. The proposal, which could be sent to Congress in a new Lula term, was articulated by Durigan as a representative of the president's re-election campaign. The topic is also supported by Labor Minister Luiz Marinho, who awaits the STF's ruling on the use of MEI for labor fraud.

item.title: Filha de Clezão, do 8 de janeiro, pede para fazer ‘visita humanitária’ a Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Ana Luiza Duarte da Cunha, daughter of Clezão — a January 8th detainee who died at the Papuda prison in 2023 — petitioned Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes for permission to make a 'humanitarian' visit to former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brasília. A candidate for district deputy running under the ballot name 'Luiza do Clezão,' she argues the meeting is part of her grieving process and pledges not to give interviews or post about it on social media. Bolsonaro is barred from receiving visitors, though Moraes has already authorized his sons Carlos and Jair Renan; Flávio Bolsonaro's visits remain suspended until October.

item.title: A Saúde nos programas de Caiado, Zema e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The provided content contains only the institutional description of Observatório das Eleições, an academic initiative coordinated by UFMG and IEPI under professor Leonardo Avritzer, which monitors electoral issues since 2018. The text does not effectively present the health proposals from the programs of Caiado, Zema, and Flávio Bolsonaro, being limited to the editorial framing of the publication. A substantive analysis of these candidates' health platforms would require access to the actual article body.

item.title: Marqueteiro de Flávio, Duda Lima passará a acompanhar candidato em viagens após sugestão de aliados
item.description: Marketing strategist Duda Lima, the third to hold the role in Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, will shift from his São Paulo headquarters-based work to traveling with the candidate across Brazil, following allies' suggestion. The change comes as Flávio expands his agenda, including his first Northeast trip to Alagoas with vice-presidential candidate Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), where he faces difficulties with local allies like JHC and Arthur Lira. The goal is to adapt Flávio's communication and discourse to different regional scenarios, such as the Northeast, where Lula leads by 28 points in the latest Datafolha poll.

item.title: Filiação ao PRTB e União Brasil: O questionamento da Justiça Eleitoral sobre a campanha de Marçal
item.description: Brazil's Electoral Public Ministry questioned the validity of Pablo Marçal's affiliation with PRTB following public statements linking him to União Brasil. Brazilian electoral law requires candidates to have their party affiliation approved and registered with the Electoral Justice at least six months before the election date. The inconsistency between public declarations and official records could jeopardize Marçal's candidacy.

item.title: Fachin recebe Janja no STF para discutir ações de combate à violência contra a mulher
item.description: STF Chief Justice Edson Fachin met with First Lady Janja Lula da Silva to discuss measures to combat feminicide and gender violence as part of the 'Todas por Todas' (All for All) pact uniting the three branches of government. During the meeting, Fachin presented CNJ results, noting that 53% of emergency protective measures are granted on the same day they reach the courts. The meeting follows an STF ruling expanding the scope of protective measures under the Maria da Penha Law to gender-based violence outside the domestic sphere.

item.title: Por que Pablo Marçal pode ‘tumultuar’ a eleição e favorecer Flávio Bolsonaro, segundo cientista político
item.description: Political scientist Elias Tavares assesses that a potential presidential run by Pablo Marçal would have more potential to disrupt the race than to take him to a runoff. According to Tavares, Marçal's strength lies in his social media mobilization and ability to create political moments, but he faces difficulties with party structure, TV time, and coalition-building. This entry could fragment the right-wing field and, paradoxically, benefit Flávio Bolsonaro by reducing pressure on the senator.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos ao governo e ao Senado em Mato Grosso
item.description: The article presents the six candidates for governor of Mato Grosso and the ten contenders for Senate in the 2026 elections, including profiles of Natasha Slhessarenko (PSD), Otaviano Pivetta (Republicans), and Rafael Milas (Mission). Brasil Real Time polls show Wellington Fagundes leading the governor's race and Mauro Mendes and Janaína Riva ahead in the Senate contest. Voters will choose two names for the Federal Senate, along with president, governor, and legislators.

item.title: A iniciativa de movimentos sociais para pressionar votação da PEC do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: The Frentes Brasil Popular and Povo Sem Medo have called for a mobilization on Sunday to pressure senators to vote on the PEC to end the 6×1 work schedule. The Senate's CCJ is expected to hold a public hearing on Tuesday, September 1st, with rapporteur Omar Aziz presenting his opinion the following day. There are still doubts about whether there will be enough time for the proposition to advance before the October elections.

item.title: A postura do governo Lula diante da revelação de mais de mil mortes na terra Yanomami
item.description: Data from the Ministry of Health reveals 1,121 deaths of Yanomami indigenous people in Lula's first three years in office, surpassing the 951 deaths recorded during the Bolsonaro administration. The government reacted with indignation at the disclosure by Veja magazine rather than addressing the humanitarian crisis, according to Senator Damares Alves, chair of the Senate Human Rights Commission. Health Minister Alexandre Padilha recorded a video defending the administration and criticizing the publication, while the Presidency labeled the analyses as 'inaccurate,' appearing more concerned with electoral impact than with the causes of deaths from malnutrition, malaria, and respiratory diseases.

item.title: Quem ganhou e quem perdeu o primeiro debate presidencial, segundo cientista político
item.description: Political scientist Elias Tavares assessed the first presidential debate, highlighting that Romeu Zema's absence was damaging since the governor needs to increase his name recognition and has low polling numbers (2% to 3%). Meanwhile, Renan Santos leveraged the opportunity to produce strategic content for social media. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, being well-positioned in the race, had a strategic justification for their absence as they had more to lose than to gain.

item.title: “Estrelas da corrupção” estão na chapa de Gaspar, diz defesa de Lulinha
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva's (Lulinha's) lawyer, Marco Aurélio Carvalho, fired back at vice-presidential candidate Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), claiming the 'true stars of corruption' are Gaspar's running mates. Carvalho accused Gaspar of having '61 million reasons to stay quiet' and of already being a suspect in court, defended Lulinha as living in Spain on his own income, and denied any connection between Lula's son and Brazil's social security institute (INSS).

item.title: ‘Todos os prefeitos do PL estão engajados na nossa campanha’, comenta Ruas sobre 'traidores' do partido no Rio
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL), candidate for Governor of Rio, stated during a rally in Praça Seca that all PL mayors are engaged in his campaign, rejecting the 'traitors' label. However, a GLOBO survey shows that nine of the 22 party mayors in the state had not publicly declared support for him. The rally was Ruas's first without Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: ‘Efeito Tarcísio’ impulsiona direita e embaralha corrida pelo Senado em São Paulo, mostra pesquisa
item.description: The 'Tarcísio effect' is strengthening right-wing candidates in the race for two Senate seats in São Paulo. Guilherme Derrite has taken the lead in the Real Time Big Data poll, surpassing Simone Tebet and Marina Silva, who had led previous surveys. However, Ricardo Salles' candidacy, with around 10% of voting intentions, could split the right-wing field and benefit opponents, according to political scientist Elias Tavares.

item.title: João Azevêdo lidera disputa pelo Senado na PB, diz Real Time Big Data
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll released on August 24, 2026, shows that former Paraíba governor João Azevêdo (PSB) leads the race for one of the state's two Senate seats with 29% of mentions, followed by Senator Veneziano Vital do Rêgo (MDB) with 23%. The survey interviewed 1,600 voters in Paraíba between August 19 and 22, has a 95% confidence level and a margin of error of 2 percentage points, and was registered with Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) under number PB-07790/2026.

item.title: Lula sugere Desenrola para clubes e comenta intervenção no Corinthians
item.description: President Lula suggested to Caixa Econômica Federal the creation of a Desenrola program specifically for football clubs, claiming teams are 'broken' due to poor management and high salaries. He also did not oppose a possible judicial intervention at Corinthians, the team he supports, conditioning the measure to proof of necessity.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro alega sátira e pede que vídeo de Lulinha siga no ar
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) legal team asked a São Paulo court to keep online an AI-generated video associating Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, with fraud against INSS retirees. The lawyers argued the content is political satire protected by free speech, noting Lulinha's name appeared in an official procedure tied to Operação Sem Desconto. Lulinha — son of President Lula, who is running for reelection — had sued to have the video removed and sought R$10,000 in moral damages.

item.title: Caso Lulinha já aparece na nova pesquisa sobre Lula x Flávio? Cientista político analisa a disputa
item.description: Political scientist Elias Tavares assesses that the revelations regarding suspicions of influence trafficking involving Lulinha, President Lula's son, represent a new risk factor for the government candidacy, but have not yet been captured by electoral polls. The race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro remains within the margin of error, with strong polarization and no room for a third alternative. The closeness between the candidates means that small shifts and new political events could be decisive in the final outcome.

item.title: Tarcísio cancela ida ao programa “Roda Viva”, da “TV Cultura”
item.description: São Paulo Governor and re-election candidate Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) canceled his appearance on TV Cultura's Roda Viva program, citing a schedule conflict. Fernando Haddad's (PT) participation remains scheduled for August 31. This is not the first time Tarcísio has refused the program, limiting direct exposure between the candidates, despite a poll showing Tarcísio with 52% versus Haddad's 35%.

item.title: Maierovitch: Lula faz jogo político e exige que Lulinha comprove inocência
item.description: Columnist Wálter Maierovitch stated on UOL News that President Lula is playing a political game by publicly demanding that his son Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, prove his innocence in ongoing investigations. According to him, Lula is trying to project a republican image while politically maneuvering around the case.

item.title: Ausência em debate pode prejudicar mais Flávio que Lula, diz especialista
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's absence from the Band presidential debate may be more damaging to him than to President Lula, according to political analyst Beto Vasques. The assessment is based on focus groups monitored during the current campaign, which suggest a negative impact among voters.

item.title: Bancos criticam trajetória da dívida e falam em até R$ 580 bi em cortes
item.description: Leaders of Brazil's major banks criticized the country's public debt trajectory, estimated at R$ 10 trillion, and urged 2026 election candidates to present fiscal proposals for the 2027-2030 period. Bradesco identified measures that could generate savings of R$ 250 billion to R$ 580 billion, depending on political will. Executives also linked high interest rates to credit costs and household indebtedness, which grew 12 percentage points over four years.

item.title: Nunes Marques deve mudar entendimento sobre deep fake após reunião com ministros do TSE
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques is expected to reconsider his position on the use of deep fakes in electoral campaigns after facing isolated defeats in the virtual plenary. Court ministers assess that he seeks to avoid further backlash by suspending rulings for 30 days to analyze the broader context. Justices appointed by former president Bolsonaro, such as Nunes Marques and Mendonça, have voted more favorably toward Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign while rejecting most requests from the Brazil of Hope Federation, which supports Lula.

item.title: "Aquela Janja": advogado aciona MP após fala de Renan Santos
item.description: A lawyer affiliated with PSol filed a criminal complaint with the Electoral Public Ministry against presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) for electoral injuria following comments about first lady Janja da Silva during a presidential debate. Renan implied that President Lula was either 'with that Janja' or 'drunk,' adding that it would be 'better to stay drunk.' The MPE will decide whether to accept the complaint and open an investigation.

item.title: Garotinho, o franco-atirador que pode levar o Rio ao segundo turno
item.description: Anthony Garotinho, running for Rio governor with Republicanos, polled at 9% in the Datafolha survey and could reach 15%, potentially forcing a runoff and disrupting Eduardo Paes's (PSD) plans, as Paes leads with 41%. Despite past convictions for administrative misconduct and the risk of having his candidacy revoked by TRE-RJ, the former governor retains significant electoral recognition. Paes's coalition has already filed a legal challenge against Garotinho's candidacy.

item.title: Novo ‘xerife’ das redes no Brasil, agência mira WhatsApp, Instagram, ChatGPT e Facebook
item.description: Brazil's data protection agency ANPD, now a regulatory body, has begun monitoring social media platforms, AI tools, and app stores to enforce compliance with the Internet Civil Framework and presidential decrees signed by Lula on protecting women online and preventing fraud. The initiative follows actions such as suspending Discord livestreams after a 13-year-old's suicide and notifying X over sexual deepfakes created via its Grok AI. Private messaging conversations remain outside the scope of oversight.

item.title: “Lulinha é estrela da corrupção”, diz Alfredo Gaspar, vice de Flávio
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), the vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket, stated that Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, is the "star of corruption." The remarks came after a Poder360 report revealed Lulinha lives in a luxury condominium in Madrid, near Brazilian football stars. Lulinha's defense rebutted the accusations, stating he lives on his own earnings and that Gaspar should remain silent.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos ao governo e ao Senado na Paraíba
item.description: The 2022 election race in Paraíba features six candidates for state governor and ten contenders for the Federal Senate. Among the gubernatorial hopefuls are Camilo Duarte (PCO), Cícero Lucena (MDB), Efraim Filho (PL), Lucas Ribeiro (PP), Pedro Coutinho (DC), and Yuri Ezequiel (UP), each with distinct political backgrounds. For the Senate, notable names include former minister Marcelo Queiroga (PL), current governor João Azevêdo (PSB), and senator Veneziano (MDB), with voters required to choose two candidates for the seats.

item.title: Lula define equipe jurídica para atuar em batalha contra Flávio Bolsonaro no TSE
item.description: President Lula and his reelection campaign coordinators have defined the legal team that will act before the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), focusing on actions involving opponent Flávio Bolsonaro, with whom they are already waging a judicial battle. The strategy reinforces the PT's preparation for the electoral and legal challenges of the upcoming race.

item.title: Público xinga Lula durante show de Gusttavo Lima em Barretos
item.description: During Globo's broadcast of the Barretos Rodeo Festival, part of the audience insulted President Lula during Gusttavo Lima's show, who did not react and continued performing. The event featured right-wing politicians including presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, congressman Nikolas Ferreira (who posed with Ana Castela showing PL's number 22), and Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, marking a strong Bolsonaro campaign act at a major cultural event in São Paulo's countryside.

item.title: O Mercosul que Milei não entende
item.description: The article harshly criticizes Argentine President Javier Milei for his attacks on President Lula and Minister Alexandre de Moraes on Brazilian soil, portraying him as a Trump proxy and far-right electoral agent. The author argues that the Lula government was right to maintain a diplomatic stance and preserve bilateral relations, emphasizing that Mercosur and the historic cooperation between Brazil and Argentina are solid and will not be destroyed by Milei.

item.title: O eleitorado que ajudou Flávio Bolsonaro a reduzir distância de Lula, segundo pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: One hundred days after the Dark Horse scandal, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) narrowed the gap with President Lula from 9 to 4 percentage points in the first round, according to the BTG/Nexus poll released on August 24. The senator rose from 33% to 37% of voting intentions, with significant gains among college-educated voters (29% to 39%), Catholics (27% to 36%), and seniors (29% to 35%). The recovery was also strategic in the Southeast and Northeast regions, where the PL candidate had been weaker.

item.title: Caiado diz que, se eleito, eleitor vai “dormir tranquilo” igual a Kassab
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) mocked his running mate Gilberto Kassab after viral footage showed him apparently napping during Band TV's first 2026 presidential debate, joking voters would 'sleep peacefully' under his presidency. Kassab denied dozing off, claiming he was using his phone. The debate was marked by the absences of Lula (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), and Romeu Zema (Novo), with only Caiado, Renan Santos (Missão), and Augusto Cury (Avante) participating.

item.title: Conheça os desafios de Lula e Flávio para conquistar o voto dos eleitores indecisos
item.description: The interview discusses the 2026 presidential race between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Dino, focusing on the key challenges each faces in winning over undecided voters. Political scientist Rodolfo Marques from the University of Amazonia analyzes the central campaign issues and how the candidates can position themselves to capture this pivotal electorate.

item.title: Nestlé não fechou fábricas nem anunciou 16 mil demissões no Brasil
item.description: False social media posts claim Nestlé shut down factories, laid off 16,000 employees, and halted KitKat production in Brazil. The company denied the allegations, which also unfairly blame the Lula government (PT) for economic issues. The disinformation aims to manipulate public perception of the crisis and federal management.

item.title: Roda Viva desta segunda-feira (24) reexibe entrevista com o ator Miguel Falabella
item.description: Roda Viva on TV Cultura aired an interview with actor Miguel Falabella instead of Tarcísio de Freitas, who had a scheduling conflict. Candidate Fernando Haddad is scheduled for August 31, following a drawing of lots attended by representatives from both campaigns.

item.title: Na campanha de Renan, Kim propõe obrigar candidatos a debates
item.description: Federal deputy Kim Kataguiri (Missão-SP), member of Renan Santos' campaign, proposed a bill to make candidates' participation in electoral debates on radio and TV mandatory. The initiative aims to increase candidate engagement in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Lula é aprovado por 55% e desaprovado por 41% na PB, diz pesquisa
item.description: A survey by Real Time Big Data conducted from August 19-22, 2026 in Paraíba shows that 55% of voters approve of President Lula's (PT) performance, while 41% disapprove. The poll interviewed 1,600 voters with a 95% confidence level and a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

item.title: Que horas começa a sabatina de Romeu Zema na Globo?
item.description: Romeu Zema's (Novo) interview on TV Globo takes place this Monday (the 24th), live from Globo Studios in Rio de Janeiro, right after Jornal Nacional, starting at 9:05 PM (Brasília time). The interview will be conducted by journalists César Tralli and Renata Vasconcellos, also broadcast on GloboNews and g1. The article also presents the full schedule of interviews with the other presidential candidates and brief profiles of each.

item.title: A culpa da ‘polarização’ é das lideranças políticas e não do povo
item.description: The article argues that political polarization in Brazil is the responsibility of political leaders, not the people. Based on a More in Common/Ipsos-Ipec survey, it shows that there is consensus between left-wing and right-wing voters on issues like work, family, and democracy, despite the distorted perception created by social media. It criticizes both PT and bolsonarism for cultivating the dehumanization of opponents, and highlights presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) as a defender of political pacification.

item.title: Quem é obrigado a votar nas eleições de 2026 e para quem o voto é facultativo
item.description: In the 2026 elections, voting is mandatory for literate Brazilians aged 18 to 70. Young people aged 16 and 17, those over 70, and illiterate individuals have optional voting and may choose whether to vote without needing to justify their absence.

item.title: Candidatos com mais de R$ 500 mil em bens recebem Bolsa Família e Gás do Povo
item.description: An Estadão investigation found at least ten candidates who declared assets over R$ 500,000 to the TSE while receiving social benefits like Bolsa Família and Gás do Povo, three of whom are millionaires, with the federal government spending over R$ 321,000 on them. Notable cases include Sérgio Francisco (DC), running for state representative in Goiás with R$ 1.2 million in assets; Talita Lemke (PDT), running for federal deputy in Goiás with R$ 1.09 million; and Mirian Moreira (PL), running for state representative in Roraima, who received R$ 46,100 in aid. The candidates cite financial hardship and inherited properties but failed to provide consistent proof of benefit cancellation.

item.title: Militares se afastam da política, mas PEC que proíbe participação das Forças está parada desde 2024
item.description: Three years after the January 8, 2023 coup-attempt riots, military candidacies dropped over 70% in the 2026 elections compared to 2022, even without the approval of the constitutional amendment that would prohibit active-duty military from running for political office. The proposal, drafted by Defense Minister José Múcio Monteiro and presented by senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA), has been stalled in Congress since 2024. Lawmakers like Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Hamilton Mourão (Republicanos-RS) criticized the measure, which would have automatically transferred military candidates to the reserves.

item.title: Eduardo endossa crítica de aliado à eleição de Michelle no DF e reacende disputa familiar
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro endorsed criticism from influencer Allan dos Santos toward Michelle Bolsonaro's Senate bid, reigniting family tensions. The video questions Michelle's viability in the DF race, favoring other candidates like Bia Kicis and Sebastião Coelho.

item.title: Lula tem 59% contra 32% de Flávio no 2º turno na PB, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll shows Lula leading with 59% against 32% for Flávio in the 2nd round in Paraíba, while Flávio faces the highest rejection rate at 52%.

item.title: PT solicita à Justiça proibição de discursos de Tarcísio em rodeios e remoção de posts sobre a Festa de Barretos
item.description: The São Paulo coalition Desperta São Paulo, composed of PT, PSB, and PSOL, filed a lawsuit with the Electoral Court demanding the removal of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' social media posts about his participation in the Barretos Country Festival, alleging the event was used for illegal electoral advertising. The lawsuit argues that the governor appropriated a third-party spectacle to gather a crowd and promote candidates, constituting a prohibited campaign rally. The coalition also requests a ban on the governor attending similar events in upcoming elections.

item.title: Conheça todos os candidatos ao Senado em 2026
item.description: In just over a month, Brazilians will go to the polls to choose 54 of the 81 seats in the Federal Senate, with 315 candidates competing for the positions nationwide. Of these, 32 are incumbent senators seeking reelection, representing more than 10% of the total. The national average is 5.8 candidates per seat, ranging from states like Alagoas (seven) to Piauí (20), and voters must select two candidates per state.
